title: openai-compat: improve function/tool calling semantics and tool schema mapping
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: The OpenAI compatibility layer must unambiguously map user-provided 'tools' to Redwood tooling semantics (tool schemas, tool_choice selection, and tool message formatting) to support function/tool calling across hosted and dedicated deployments. This PR implements a deterministic schema mapper, clarifies 'tool_choice' semantics in the runtime, and stabilizes streaming behavior when a model returns a tool call. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces a tool_schema_mapper that flattens and normalizes OpenAI-like tool definitions into Redwood tool descriptors (input_schema -> json-schema normalizer, required/optional fields, typed args). 2) Enforces tool_choice semantics: when the model selects a tool via 'tool_choice' we now resolve against the mapped tool set by exact name match, then by case-insensitive fallback, and finally by deterministic alias matching defined in the mapper. 3) Ensures tool messages are emitted as structured JSON messages on the streaming channel (event types: tool_call.start, tool_call.data, tool_call.finish) so downstream clients and SDKs can rehydrate tool invocations reliably. 4) Adds integration tests for edge cases: missing required args, multiple candidate tools with same name, tool_choice null, and streaming interruptions. 5) Updates SDK surface notes and redwood-docs/openai/compatibility.md with examples and migration guidance. Compatibility notes: default behavior remains backward-compatible for typical usages; users relying on ambiguous name matching should test with the new deterministic alias rules. Rollout: feature gated behind OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOL_CALLING flag and a gradual rollout to production (10% -> 50% -> 100%) after monitoring metrics described below. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs updated - [x] feature flag added - [x] benchmarked (1.2% CPU regression in worst-case but improved tail latency for tool-heavy workloads). Testing/Observability: added spans for tool resolution, metrics:工具_resolve_time_ms, tool_stream_retries, tool_messages_emitted, and a dashboard in Redwood Console under "OpenAI Compatibility / Tool Calling". Migration: operators can enable the feature flag per-customer; no schema migration needed for stored tool definitions but clients that depend on fuzzy name matching should validate.

release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: deterministic tool schema mapping and alias resolution
Streaming: tool_call events are now structured and emitted during streaming responses
Behavior: deterministic tool_choice semantics; ambiguous name matching now uses explicit alias table
testing_notes: Unit and integration coverage added. Integration suite includes simulated model responses for tool_choice variants and stream interruption/resume. Added e2e test in perf-canary to validate streaming formatting under load. QA checklist executed on staging with feature flag enabled for a customer subset.
migration_instructions: No persistent schema migration required. Operators should enable OPENAI_COMPAT_TOOL_CALLING flag and validate client behavior for any fuzzy-matching assumptions. If your clients relied on case-insensitive fuzzy name matching, add aliases in the tool registration metadata now to preserve behavior.
compatibility_notes: Backwards-compatible for typical tool calling. Deterministic alias rules may change observed selection for previously-ambiguous tool names; we recommend customers run compatibility tests before enabling the flag at 100%.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated. Rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with monitoring on tool_resolve_time_ms and tool_stream_retries. If tool_stream_retries > 0.5% or tool_messages_emitted drops > 5% rollback immediately.
